passages.text: A good name is better than fine perfume, and one’s day of death is better than his day of birth.
passages.sermon:
A good name is valuable.
A good name is better than fine perfume.
The day of death is important.
The day of death is better than the day of birth.
passages.original: ט֥וֹב שֵׁ֖ם מִשֶּׁ֣מֶן ט֑וֹב וְי֣וֹם הַמָּ֔וֶת מִיּ֖וֹם הִוָּלְדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: It is better to enter a house of mourning than a house of feasting, since death is the end of every man, and the living should take this to heart.
passages.sermon:
Every person will die.
Death is the end for all people.
A house of mourning is a place where people grieve for the dead.
A house of feasting is a place where people celebrate and enjoy themselves.
It is better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting.
The living should remember this truth about death.
The living should take this lesson to heart.
passages.original: ט֞וֹב לָלֶ֣כֶת אֶל־ בֵּֽית־ אֵ֗בֶל מִלֶּ֙כֶת֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה בַּאֲשֶׁ֕ר ה֖וּא ס֣וֹף כָּל־ הָאָדָ֑ם וְהַחַ֖י יִתֵּ֥ן אֶל־ לִבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Sorrow is better than laughter, for a sad countenance is good for the heart.
passages.sermon: Sorrow is better than laughter.\r\nA sad face helps the heart.\r\nA sad countenance brings good to the heart.
passages.original: ט֥וֹב כַּ֖עַס מִשְּׂחֹ֑ק כִּֽי־ בְרֹ֥עַ פָּנִ֖ים יִ֥יטַב לֵֽב׃

passages.text: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.
passages.sermon:
A wise person thinks about sorrow and loss.
A wise person spends time in places where people mourn.
A foolish person thinks about pleasure and fun.
A foolish person spends time in places of celebration.
passages.original: לֵ֤ב חֲכָמִים֙ בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔בֶל וְלֵ֥ב כְּסִילִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית שִׂמְחָֽה׃

passages.text: It is better to heed a wise man’s rebuke than to listen to the song of fools.
passages.sermon:
A wise man gives a rebuke.
A rebuke is a correction or warning.
A fool sings a song.
A song of fools is empty and meaningless.
It is better to listen to a wise man’s rebuke.
It is not good to listen to the song of fools.
passages.original: ט֕וֹב לִשְׁמֹ֖עַ גַּעֲרַ֣ת חָכָ֑ם מֵאִ֕ישׁ שֹׁמֵ֖עַ שִׁ֥יר כְּסִילִֽים׃

passages.text: For like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This too is futile.
passages.sermon:
The laughter of a fool is loud and empty.
It sounds like thorns crackling under a pot.
This laughter is pointless.
It has no lasting value.
It is futile.
passages.original: כִּ֣י כְק֤וֹל הַסִּירִים֙ תַּ֣חַת הַסִּ֔יר כֵּ֖ן שְׂחֹ֣ק הַכְּסִ֑יל וְגַם־ זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃

passages.text: Surely extortion turns a wise man into a fool, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
passages.sermon:
A wise man knows what is right.
Extortion can confuse a wise man.
Extortion can make a wise man act foolishly.
A bribe can destroy a person’s heart.
A bribe can lead a person away from what is right.
passages.original: כִּ֥י הָעֹ֖שֶׁק יְהוֹלֵ֣ל חָכָ֑ם וִֽיאַבֵּ֥ד אֶת־ לֵ֖ב מַתָּנָֽה׃

passages.text: The end of a matter is better than the beginning, and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.
passages.sermon:
This passage comes from Ecclesiastes. The writer is a wise teacher. He compares the end and the beginning of things. He also compares patience and pride.\r\n
The end of a matter is better than its beginning.\r\n
A patient spirit is better than a proud spirit.
passages.original: ט֛וֹב אַחֲרִ֥ית דָּבָ֖ר מֵֽרֵאשִׁית֑וֹ ט֥וֹב אֶֽרֶךְ־ ר֖וּחַ מִגְּבַהּ־ רֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger settles in the lap of a fool.
passages.sermon:
A fool lets anger rest in his heart.
Do not let your spirit become angry quickly.
Anger belongs with fools.
Do not let anger control you.
passages.original: אַל־ תְּבַהֵ֥ל בְּרֽוּחֲךָ֖ לִכְע֑וֹס כִּ֣י כַ֔עַס בְּחֵ֥יק כְּסִילִ֖ים יָנֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?” For it is unwise of you to ask about this.
passages.sermon: Do not say, "Why were the old days better than these?"\r\nIt is unwise to ask this question.\r\nYou do not ask this from wisdom.
passages.original: אַל־ תֹּאמַר֙ מֶ֣ה הָיָ֔ה שֶׁ֤הַיָּמִים֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנִ֔ים הָי֥וּ טוֹבִ֖ים מֵאֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֛י לֹ֥א מֵחָכְמָ֖ה שָׁאַ֥לְתָּ עַל־ זֶֽה׃

passages.text: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is good, and it benefits those who see the sun.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is good.
Inheritance is good.
Wisdom is like an inheritance.
Wisdom helps people who are alive.
People who see the sun are living people.
Wisdom gives benefit to living people.
passages.original: טוֹבָ֥ה חָכְמָ֖ה עִֽם־ נַחֲלָ֑ה וְיֹתֵ֖ר לְרֹאֵ֥י הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

passages.text: For wisdom, like money, is a shelter, and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom protects a person.
Money also protects a person.
Wisdom gives a person knowledge.
Wisdom keeps its owner alive.
passages.original: כִּ֛י בְּצֵ֥ל הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה בְּצֵ֣ל הַכָּ֑סֶף וְיִתְר֣וֹן דַּ֔עַת הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה תְּחַיֶּ֥ה בְעָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Consider the work of God: Who can straighten what He has bent?
passages.sermon:
God acts with power and authority.
God creates and shapes all things.
Look at what God has done.
No one can change what God has made crooked.
No one can fix what God has bent.
God’s work cannot be undone by people.
passages.original: רְאֵ֖ה אֶת־ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּ֣י מִ֤י יוּכַל֙ לְתַקֵּ֔ן אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִוְּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: In the day of prosperity, be joyful, but in the day of adversity, consider this: God has made one of these along with the other, so that a man cannot discover anything that will come after him.
passages.sermon:
God rules over all things.
God creates both good days and bad days.
When you have a good day, rejoice.
When you have a bad day, pay attention.
God made both kinds of days.
God did this so that people cannot know what will happen in the future.
passages.original: בְּי֤וֹם טוֹבָה֙ הֱיֵ֣ה בְט֔וֹב וּבְי֥וֹם רָעָ֖ה רְאֵ֑ה גַּ֣ם אֶת־ זֶ֤ה לְעֻמַּת־ זֶה֙ עָשָׂ֣ה הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים עַל־ דִּבְרַ֗ת שֶׁלֹּ֨א יִמְצָ֧א הָֽאָדָ֛ם אַחֲרָ֖יו מְאֽוּמָה׃

passages.text: In my futile life I have seen both of these: A righteous man perishing in his righteousness, and a wicked man living long in his wickedness.
passages.sermon:
I have lived a life that feels futile.
I have seen many things in my days.
I saw a righteous man.
He died even though he was righteous.
I saw a wicked man.
He lived a long time in his wickedness.
passages.original: אֶת־ הַכֹּ֥ל רָאִ֖יתִי בִּימֵ֣י הֶבְלִ֑י יֵ֤שׁ צַדִּיק֙ אֹבֵ֣ד בְּצִדְק֔וֹ וְיֵ֣שׁ רָשָׁ֔ע מַאֲרִ֖יךְ בְּרָעָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
passages.sermon:
This passage gives advice to people who want to live wisely.
Do not try to be too righteous.
Do not try to be too wise.
If you do these things, you may harm yourself.
You may destroy yourself by going too far.
passages.original: אַל־ תְּהִ֤י צַדִּיק֙ הַרְבֵּ֔ה וְאַל־ תִּתְחַכַּ֖ם יוֹתֵ֑ר לָ֖מָּה תִּשּׁוֹמֵֽם׃

passages.text: Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?
passages.sermon:
God warns people in this verse.
He says, “Do not be very wicked.”
He also says, “Do not be a fool.”
If you are very wicked, you bring harm to yourself.
If you act foolishly, you put yourself in danger.
If you do these things, you may die before your time.
God does not want you to die early because of your own actions.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּרְשַׁ֥ע הַרְבֵּ֖ה וְאַל־ תְּהִ֣י סָכָ֑ל לָ֥מָּה תָמ֖וּת בְּלֹ֥א עִתֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: It is good to grasp the one and not let the other slip from your hand. For he who fears God will follow both warnings.
passages.sermon:
A person should hold on to what is good.
A person should not let go of what is right.
A person who fears God will obey both instructions.
A person who fears God will avoid both extremes.
passages.original: ט֚וֹב אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֶּאֱחֹ֣ז בָּזֶ֔ה וְגַם־ מִזֶּ֖ה אַל־ תַּנַּ֣ח אֶת־ יָדֶ֑ךָ כִּֽי־ יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים יֵצֵ֥א אֶת־ כֻּלָּֽם׃

passages.text: Wisdom makes the wise man stronger than ten rulers in a city.
passages.sermon: A wise man has wisdom.\r\nWisdom gives him strength.\r\nHe becomes stronger than ten rulers in a city.
passages.original: הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה תָּעֹ֣ז לֶחָכָ֑ם מֵֽעֲשָׂרָה֙ שַׁלִּיטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ בָּעִֽיר׃

passages.text: Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.
passages.sermon: No person on earth is completely righteous.\r\nNo one always does good.\r\nNo one never sins.
passages.original: כִּ֣י אָדָ֔ם אֵ֥ין צַדִּ֖יק בָּאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲשֶׂה־ טּ֖וֹב וְלֹ֥א יֶחֱטָֽא׃

passages.text: Do not pay attention to every word that is spoken, or you may hear your servant cursing you.
passages.sermon: Do not pay attention to every word people say.\r\nYou may hear your servant curse you.
passages.original: גַּ֤ם לְכָל־ הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ אַל־ תִּתֵּ֖ן לִבֶּ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ תִשְׁמַ֥ע אֶֽת־ עַבְדְּךָ֖ מְקַלְלֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: For you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others.
passages.sermon: You know this in your heart.\r\nYou have cursed other people many times.\r\nYou have done this yourself.
passages.original: כִּ֛י גַּם־ פְּעָמִ֥ים רַבּ֖וֹת יָדַ֣ע לִבֶּ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר גַּם־ אַתְּ קִלַּ֥לְתָּ אֲחֵרִֽים׃

passages.text: All this I tested by wisdom, saying, “I resolve to be wise.” But it was beyond me.
passages.sermon:
I am the speaker in this passage.  
I used wisdom to test everything I saw.  
I said, "I will become wise."  
But wisdom was far from me.  
I could not reach it.
passages.original: כָּל־ זֹ֖ה נִסִּ֣יתִי בַֽחָכְמָ֑ה אָמַ֣רְתִּי אֶחְכָּ֔מָה וְהִ֖יא רְחוֹקָ֥ה מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

passages.text: What exists is out of reach and very deep. Who can fathom it?
passages.sermon:
The Teacher speaks about wisdom and understanding.
He says, “What has happened is far away.”
He says, “What exists is hard to reach.”
He says, “It is very deep.”
He asks, “Who can find it?”
passages.original: רָח֖וֹק מַה־ שֶּׁהָיָ֑ה וְעָמֹ֥ק׀ עָמֹ֖ק מִ֥י יִמְצָאֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: I directed my mind to understand, to explore, to search out wisdom and explanations, and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the folly of madness.
passages.sermon:
I am the Teacher.
I wanted to understand many things.
I set my heart to know and to search.
I looked for wisdom.
I looked for reasons and explanations.
I wanted to understand why people do evil things.
I wanted to see the foolishness of wickedness.
I wanted to see the madness of foolish acts.
passages.original: סַבּ֨וֹתִֽי אֲנִ֤י וְלִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת וְלָת֔וּר וּבַקֵּ֥שׁ חָכְמָ֖ה וְחֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן וְלָדַ֙עַת֙ רֶ֣שַׁע כֶּ֔סֶל וְהַסִּכְל֖וּת הוֹלֵלֽוֹת׃

passages.text: And I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a net, and whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is ensnared.
passages.sermon:
The Teacher speaks.
He says, “I find a certain woman is more bitter than death.
This woman is a snare.
Her heart is like a net.
Her hands are like chains.
A man who pleases God escapes from her.
A sinner is caught by her.”
passages.original: וּמוֹצֶ֨א אֲנִ֜י מַ֣ר מִמָּ֗וֶת אֶת־ הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁר־ הִ֨יא מְצוֹדִ֧ים וַחֲרָמִ֛ים לִבָּ֖הּ אֲסוּרִ֣ים יָדֶ֑יהָ ט֞וֹב לִפְנֵ֤י הָאֱלֹהִים֙ יִמָּלֵ֣ט מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְחוֹטֵ֖א יִלָּ֥כֶד בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: “Behold,” says the Teacher, “I have discovered this by adding one thing to another to find an explanation.
passages.sermon:
The Teacher speaks.
The Teacher says, “Look, I have found something.”
I discovered this by adding one thing to another.
I did this to find an explanation.
passages.original: רְאֵה֙ זֶ֣ה מָצָ֔אתִי אָמְרָ֖ה קֹהֶ֑לֶת אַחַ֥ת לְאַחַ֖ת לִמְצֹ֥א חֶשְׁבּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: While my soul was still searching but not finding, among a thousand I have found one upright man, but among all these I have not found one such woman.
passages.sermon:
The Teacher is searching for upright people.
The Teacher’s soul keeps searching.
The Teacher does not find what he seeks.
Among a thousand men, the Teacher finds one upright man.
Among all these, the Teacher does not find one upright woman.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֛ר עוֹד־ בִּקְשָׁ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֖י וְלֹ֣א מָצָ֑אתִי אָדָ֞ם אֶחָ֤ד מֵאֶ֙לֶף֙ מָצָ֔אתִי וְאִשָּׁ֥ה בְכָל־ אֵ֖לֶּה לֹ֥א מָצָֽאתִי׃

passages.text: Only this have I found: I have discovered that God made men upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”
passages.sermon:
God made people upright.
God created humans to be good.
People have searched for many schemes.
People have chosen many plans of their own.
passages.original: לְבַד֙ רְאֵה־ זֶ֣ה מָצָ֔אתִי אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֧ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־ הָאָדָ֖ם יָשָׁ֑ר וְהֵ֥מָּה בִקְשׁ֖וּ חִשְּׁבֹנ֥וֹת רַבִּֽים׃
